Babylon 5 takes a little while to warm up, but once it gets going the writing is awesome. It has long complicated story arcs that span multiple seasons, interspersed with shorter stories than span single or multiple episodes. It doesn't really "grow a beard" until Commander Sinclair leaves and is replaced with Commander Sheridan in season 2.

The only problem with the long intertwined story arcs, is that you can't really just watch one episode out of sequence, without context it loses a lot of its depth. That's probably why it hasn't been re-run as much as it deserves.

It's greatest weakness is it's visuals.. It was made at the same time as Star Trek DS9. And was one of the first TV shows to rely heavily on CGI special effects (particularly for spacecraft etc). At the time these effects were amazing, they were movie quality special effects on a weekly TV show. However watching the show now, in comparison to the CGI spacecraft we've become used to in shows like BattleStar Galactica etc, the CGI in Babylon 5 looks like a cutscene in an indie computer game. But if you can cope with the 1960's special effects in Star Trek, I'm sure you can cope with the 20 year old special effects in B5.

Yup, the visuals are a little tatty. They were actually made on an Amiga using a 'Video toaster' add on.

However, don't let that put you off, as the writing is great after once season 2 gets going, and the story is genuinely compelling and thrilling.

John Sheridan is one of my all time favorite heroes; Courageous, charming, moral and decent, but terrifyingly single-minded once he works up a righteous anger. If he were real I would follow that man into hell itself.

The Psycho Pass is a good smart sci-fi taking place in strange totality. The system seems to have eliminated poverty and crime - yet dictates very large amount of your future. The state gives you job options based on your results - not market. People do not have much freedom in career, but they have absolute job security. Similarly, the crime is almost absent, but the price is horrendous - governing bodies lock up people who have only potential to commit crime based on their psychological profile (Psycho-Pass), not based on the guilt of the finished deed.

The protagonist is a rookie policewoman of strange mental robustness.

The show has a lot of interesting themes about roles of governing bodies, personal responsibility and role of subversion. Where do you turn if your masters punish people for crimes they only may commit in the future and your enemies are seeding chaos and destruction? Is there actually real free will if we are predisposed by genetics and surroundings? Should society maximize freedom or happiness?

The character ark is very much "storytelling 101," but it is masterfully done. There is a lot of foreshadowing, so do not search much about the show and enjoy deciphering the clues for yourself.

Also, there is the killer soundtrack that pumps your blood and makes you want to go running, jumping on cars and shooting people.
